source.check: Unopposed nominations from the Derry Journal (20 September 1946, p. 7).

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 3 October 1946. Twenty-four candidates were returned unopposed for the 28 seats, three retiring members were automatically returned in divisions with no nominations, and Lislea, reported in the nominations as a contest, was settled without a poll: the Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Strabane Chronicle, 28 September 1946, p. 2) declares Dunn elected there, no poll having been taken. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Deoratt' to Doorat (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1925-69 name the DED Doorat; the rounds were filed as Dooratt (1927); Doorat (1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1958, 1961, 1964, 1967); Deoratt (1946). This round was filed as 'Deoratt', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (deoratt) answers with a redirect to this one.
